name: Venomancer: Poisonous and Corrosion Nature damage modifiers (#3124, #3318)
contract: #3124, #3318. Poisonous 707320 (Spell.dbc, passive): effect 0 is aura 237 MOD_SPELL_DAMAGE_OF_ATTACK_POWER, misc 126 (all magic schools), 29+1 = 30% of attack power, read by Unit::SpellBaseDamageBonusDone (Unit.cpp:9592); effect 1 is aura 286 ABILITY_PERIODIC_CRIT with class mask [0,0,0x4] = Expulsion 805094 and its ranks, read by AuraEffect::CalcPeriodicCritChance (SpellAuraEffects.cpp:1167). The 30% is asserted through spell_power (Nature, school 3) against the pre-learn value in the same run and against an untalented control; the periodic crit through the snapshotted crit chance of a real Expulsion aura on a dummy, the control's aura carrying 0. Corrosion 803194: effect 0 is aura 87 MOD_DAMAGE_PERCENT_TAKEN, misc 8 (Nature), 4+1 = 5; the dummy's incoming Nature damage from the caster (fixed base 1000) must be 5% above its own pre-cast value. Expulsion and Corrosion require Beetle Form 803183 (Spell.dbc CasterAuraSpell) and Rage. Unverified assumption: a class 29 fixture can hold 200 Rage via set_power. Expulsion's own effect 0 (Spell.dbc) targets TARGET_SRC_CASTER/TARGET_UNIT_SRC_AREA_ENEMY (implicitTargetA 22, implicitTargetB 15) -- it is an AoE around the caster, not the explicit unit target the cast packet carries -- so it also hits the other player's dummy when both are near each other; v's cast is asserted (landing + crit) before c ever casts, so c's later cast cannot overwrite v's non-stacking aura on dv first. Expulsion's DmgClass (Spell.dbc) is 2 (SPELL_DAMAGE_CLASS_MELEE), so AuraEffect::CalcPeriodicCritChance routes its crit chance through Unit::SpellDoneCritChance's melee branch (PLAYER_CRIT_PERCENTAGE, driven by CR_CRIT_MELEE), not the spell-crit branch; both fixtures also carry melee_crit_rating so v's snapshotted crit is provably positive while c's stays 0 because CalcPeriodicCritChance only looks at it once c is found to hold no SPELL_AURA_ABILITY_PERIODIC_CRIT effect (Poisonous is never learned by c). Generic core machinery: a regression guard for behaviour that already works.
